self_contained_problem:
Let $I=(c,d)$ with $-\infty\le c<0<d\le\infty$, and let $w:I\to(0,\infty)$ be an admissible exponential weight in the following sense. Write $Q=\log(1/w)$ and assume:

(i) $Q$ is continuously differentiable on $I$ with $Q(0)=0$;
(ii) $Q'$ is nondecreasing on $I$, and $Q(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to c^+$ and as $x\to d^-$;
(iii) the function $T(x)=xQ'(x)/Q(x)$ ($x\ne0$) is quasi-increasing on $(0,d)$ and quasi-decreasing on $(c,0)$, and satisfies $T(x)\ge\lambda>1$ for all $x\ne 0$;
(iv) there exists $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1)$ such that $T(y)\sim T\!\left(y\bigl(1-\varepsilon_0/T(y)\bigr)\right)$ for $y\ne 0$;
(v) for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that
$$\int_{x-\delta x/T(x)}^{x+\delta x/T(x)}\frac{|Q'(s)-Q'(x)|}{|s-x|^{3/2}}\,ds\;\le\;\varepsilon\,|Q'(x)|\sqrt{T(x)/|x|}\qquad(x\ne 0).$$

For each $n\ge 1$ fix an array $\chi_n=\{x_{1,n},\dots,x_{n,n}\}\subset I$ of distinct interpolation nodes together with positive "Cotes numbers" $\{\lambda_{j,n}\}_{j=1}^n$. Let $V:I\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth weight factor that decays at the endpoints $c$ and $d$, let $0<p<\infty$, and let $\mathcal P_{n-1}$ denote the algebraic polynomials of degree at most $n-1$.

$$\sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_{j,n}\, w(x_{j,n})^{-2}\,V(x_{j,n})\,|P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p \;\le\; C\int_I |P(x)w(x)|^p\,V(x)\,dx;$$

(b) Converse Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund estimate
$$\|Pw\|_{L^p(I)} \;\le\; C\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_{j,n}\, w(x_{j,n})^{-2}\,|P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p\Bigr)^{1/p}.$$

(c) Establish corresponding polynomial density criteria, in particular characterizing those continuous $f$ for which weighted polynomial approximation $\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\|(f-P)w\|$ tends to $0$, including endpoint-decay conditions on $fw/V$.

(d) Apply the resulting estimates to prove mean ($L^p$) and uniform convergence of Lagrange interpolation operators at the nodes $\chi_n$ and of orthogonal expansions with respect to $w^2$, and to obtain quantitative rates of convergence.

paper_title: Tree Spanners on Chordal Graphs: Complexity, Algorithms, Open Problems
original_question: Given a connected graph G, a spanning tree T is a tree 3-spanner when every pair of vertices x and y has tree distance d_T(x, y) at most 3 times graph distance d_G(x, y). A graph is chordal when it has no chordless cycle of length at least four, and a graph is strongly chordal when it is chordal and has no induced k-sun for any k >= 3. Is there an efficient algorithm to decide whether a chordal graph, and in particular whether a strongly chordal graph, admits a tree 3-spanner?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. For vertices x, y ∈ V, let d_G(x, y) denote the length (number of edges) of a shortest path between x and y in G. A spanning tree T of G is called a tree 3-spanner of G if, for every pair of vertices x, y ∈ V, the distance d_T(x, y) in T satisfies d_T(x, y) ≤ 3 · d_G(x, y).

A graph is chordal if it contains no induced cycle of length at least 4. For an integer k ≥ 3, a k-sun is the graph on 2k vertices consisting of a cycle u_1, w_1, u_2, w_2, …, u_k, w_k, u_1 together with all edges of a clique on {u_1, …, u_k}, where each w_i has degree exactly 2. A graph is strongly chordal if it is chordal and contains no induced k-sun for any k ≥ 3.

The Tree 3-Spanner problem on a graph class C asks: given G ∈ C, decide whether G admits a tree 3-spanner.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that decides Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is chordal? In particular, does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm deciding Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is strongly chordal?
status_search_result: Searches indicate the complexity of deciding Tree 3-Spanner on chordal graphs, and even on the subclass of strongly chordal (undirected path) graphs, is still listed as an open problem. Positive polynomial-time results are known for several subclasses (very strongly chordal graphs, 1-split graphs, interval graphs, split graphs, chordal graphs of diameter ≤ 2, chordal bipartite graphs, etc.), and Tree t-Spanner is known to be NP-complete on chordal graphs for t ≥ 4, but no resolution of the t = 3 case on chordal/strongly chordal graphs was found.

context_brief: Chordal graphs of diameter at most t
original_question: For an integer t >= 3, what is the computational complexity of deciding whether a chordal graph G with diameter at most t admits a tree t-spanner, that is, a spanning tree preserving all graph distances up to multiplicative stretch t?
self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. The distance d_G(u,v) between two vertices u,v∈V is the number of edges on a shortest u–v path in G, and the diameter of G is max_{u,v∈V} d_G(u,v). A graph is chordal if every cycle of length at least 4 has a chord (an edge joining two non-consecutive vertices of the cycle). For an integer t≥1, a tree t-spanner of G is a spanning tree T of G such that d_T(u,v) ≤ t · d_G(u,v) for every pair of vertices u,v∈V; equivalently (for unweighted graphs), d_T(u,v) ≤ t whenever {u,v}∈E.

The Tree t-Spanner problem asks, given a graph G, whether G admits a tree t-spanner.

Problem. Fix an integer t≥3. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given a chordal graph G of diameter at most t, decide whether G admits a tree t-spanner.
status_search_result: Known results show that for t≥4 Tree t-Spanner is NP-complete on chordal graphs of diameter at most t+1 (t even) or t+2 (t odd), and is solvable in linear time on chordal graphs of diameter at most t−1 (t even) or t−2 (t odd). The complexity of Tree 3-Spanner on chordal graphs remains open in general, and the boundary case of chordal graphs of diameter exactly t (the smallest unresolved diameter for each t≥3) is not resolved in the published literature.

paper_title: A Collection of Open Problems
context_brief: Asymptotic enumeration of labeled C4-free graphs.
original_question: Let C4 denote the 4-cycle, and let f(n; C4) be the number of labeled graphs on n vertices that do not contain C4 as a subgraph. Is it true that f(n; C4) = 2^((1/2 + o(1)) n^(3/2)) as n tends to infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $C_4$ denote the cycle on four vertices. For a positive integer $n$, let $f(n;C_4)$ denote the number of labeled simple graphs on the vertex set $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ that contain no copy of $C_4$ as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph. Determine whether
$$f(n;C_4) = 2^{\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1)\right) n^{3/2}}\qquad\text{as } n\to\infty.$$
Equivalently, is it true that $\log_2 f(n;C_4) \sim \tfrac{1}{2} n^{3/2}$?
status_search_result: The lower bound $f(n;C_4)\ge 2^{\mathrm{ex}(n,C_4)}=2^{(1/2+o(1))n^{3/2}}$ is immediate from extremal $C_4$-free graphs, and Kleitman–Winston proved an upper bound of the form $2^{c\,n^{3/2}}$ for some constant $c$, but the matching constant $c=1/2$ remains unproven. Surveys on enumeration of $H$-free graphs for bipartite $H$ continue to list this as open: even the correct constant in the exponent for $C_4$-free graphs is not known.

paper_title: Open problems on Iwahori-Hecke algebras
context_brief: Associativity of the asymptotic Hecke algebra
original_question: Assume the boundedness hypothesis that there is an integer N >= 0 such that v^{-N} h_{x,y,z} is in Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y, z in W, where the basis elements c_w satisfy c_x c_y = sum_{z in W} h_{x,y,z} c_z. For each z in W, let a(z) be the unique integer >= 0 such that every h_{x,y,z} lies in v^{a(z)} Z[v^{-1}] and, for at least one pair x, y, the same coefficient h_{x,y,z} does not lie in v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]. Define integers gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} by h_{x,y,z} = gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} v^{a(z)} modulo v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]. Let J be the free abelian group with basis {t_w : w in W}, and define multiplication on basis elements by t_x t_y = sum_{z in W} gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} t_z. Does this multiplication make J into an associative ring, not necessarily with an identity element?
self_contained_problem:
Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system with weight function L, and let H be the associated Iwahori–Hecke algebra over Z[v,v^{-1}] with Kazhdan–Lusztig basis {c_w : w ∈ W}. Write the structure constants

  c_x c_y = Σ_{z ∈ W} h_{x,y,z} c_z,   h_{x,y,z} ∈ Z[v,v^{-1}].

Assume the boundedness hypothesis: there exists an integer N ≥ 0 such that v^{-N} h_{x,y,z} ∈ Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y, z ∈ W.

For each z ∈ W, define a(z) to be the unique nonnegative integer such that
 (i) h_{x,y,z} ∈ v^{a(z)} Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y ∈ W, and
 (ii) there exist x, y ∈ W with h_{x,y,z} ∉ v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}].

Define integers γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} ∈ Z by the congruence
  h_{x,y,z} ≡ γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} v^{a(z)}  (mod v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]).

Let J be the free abelian group with basis {t_w : w ∈ W}, and define a Z-bilinear product on J by
  t_x t_y = Σ_{z ∈ W} γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} t_z.

Question: Does this product endow J with the structure of an associative ring (not required to have a multiplicative identity)?
status_search_result: Associativity of J is known to follow from Lusztig's conjectures P1–P15, and these conjectures are established in significant cases (e.g., equal-parameter finite and affine Weyl groups, and certain other settings) where boundedness is known. However, for general Coxeter groups with arbitrary positive weight function, P1–P15 — and hence the associativity of J in full generality — remain open. Recent work (e.g., on boundedness of the a-function for Coxeter groups of finite rank) extends the cases where the construction is valid, but the question is not settled in full generality.

paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
original_question: How can phase-type distributions be characterized using only the Laplace transform of their probability density? A phase-type distribution is an absorption-time distribution for a finite-state absorbing Markov chain. The known characterization cited in the source says that a nonzero distribution on [0,infinity) is phase-type exactly when it has a rational Laplace transform with a unique pole of maximal real part and its probability density is positive on [0,infinity); the open problem is to replace this mixed s-domain and t-domain criterion by a condition stated solely in terms of the Laplace transform.
self_contained_problem:
A phase-type distribution is the probability distribution of the absorption time of a continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space with one absorbing state and the remaining states transient, started from some initial distribution on the transient states. Equivalently, on (0,∞) such a distribution has density f(t) = α e^{tT} (-T) 1, where T is a sub-generator (an n×n matrix with negative diagonal, nonnegative off-diagonal entries, and nonpositive row sums, at least one strict) and α is a sub-probability row vector on {1,...,n}.

A classical theorem states that a nonzero probability distribution on [0,∞) is phase-type if and only if:
(i) its Laplace transform F(s) = ∫₀^∞ e^{-st} f(t) dt is a rational function of s, with a unique pole of maximal real part; and
(ii) its probability density f(t) is strictly positive for all t ∈ (0,∞).

This characterization mixes an s-domain condition (i) with a t-domain condition (ii). The problem is the following:

Find necessary and sufficient conditions, stated purely in terms of the Laplace transform F(s) (i.e., purely in the s-domain, without reference to positivity properties of the time-domain density f(t)), under which a probability distribution on [0,∞) is phase-type.
status_search_result: Standard references (including the Wikipedia summary and survey/working papers on phase-type distributions) state the same mixed s-domain/t-domain characterization (rational Laplace transform with unique pole of maximal real part plus positive density on (0,∞)). No purely Laplace-transform-based characterization appears in the literature found; the problem of replacing the positive-density condition with an equivalent s-domain condition is still cited as open.

paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
original_question: What general properties can be proved about the zero locations, or the relative pole and zero locations, of the Laplace transform of a phase-type distribution? The setting is the Laplace transform of the probability density of a phase-type distribution; known eigenvalue results constrain possible pole locations because poles of the transform are eigenvalues of the generator matrix T in any phase-type representation, but the analogous general information about zeros remains unknown.
self_contained_problem:
A phase-type (PH) distribution on $[0,\infty)$ is the distribution of the absorption time of a continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $\{1,\dots,n,n+1\}$ in which state $n+1$ is absorbing and states $1,\dots,n$ are transient. Such a chain is specified by an initial probability row vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $\alpha\mathbf{1}\le 1$) on the transient states and a subgenerator matrix $T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ whose off-diagonal entries are nonnegative, whose row sums are nonpositive, and which is nonsingular (so that absorption occurs almost surely). The pair $(\alpha,T)$ is called a PH-representation of order $n$. The associated probability density function on $(0,\infty)$ is
$$f(t)=\alpha\, e^{tT}\,(-T)\mathbf{1},$$
and its Laplace transform is the rational function
$$\widehat f(s)=\int_0^\infty e^{-st}f(t)\,dt=\alpha\,(sI-T)^{-1}(-T)\mathbf{1}.$$
It is known that the poles of $\widehat f(s)$ lie among the eigenvalues of $T$, hence in the open left half-plane, and that for any PH-representation the dominant (rightmost) eigenvalue of $T$ is a real negative number that is a pole of $\widehat f$.

Establish general structural properties of the zeros of $\widehat f(s)$, or of the relative locations of the poles and zeros of $\widehat f(s)$, that hold for every phase-type distribution. In particular, determine which regions of the complex plane can contain zeros of $\widehat f(s)$, and identify any interlacing, separation, or sign constraints between poles and zeros that follow from the PH structure (nonnegativity of off-diagonal entries of $T$, nonpositive row sums, and nonnegativity of $\alpha$).
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a general theorem characterizing the zero locations, or pole/zero interlacing properties, of Laplace transforms of phase-type distributions. While pole locations are well understood via eigenvalues of the subgenerator $T$, no comparable general results about zeros appear to be available in the literature, consistent with the problem being posed as an open question.

paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
context_brief: Minimal order for one real and one complex pole pair
original_question: For phase-type distributions with Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=1/q(s), where q(s)=(1+s/c)(1+s/(a+ib))(1+s/(a-ib)) and a,b,c are positive real parameters, suppose the eigenvalue-angle condition for phase-type generators gives a lower bound n_min on the possible order of any representation. Does there always exist a phase-type representation of exactly order n_min for every such distribution?
self_contained_problem:
A continuous phase-type (PH) distribution is the distribution of the absorption time of a continuous-time Markov chain on the state space {1,...,n,n+1}, where state n+1 is absorbing and states 1,...,n are transient. Such a distribution is characterized by a pair (α, T), called a representation of order n, where α is a 1×n nonnegative row vector with α·1 ≤ 1 (the initial distribution on transient states) and T is an n×n sub-generator matrix (off-diagonal entries nonnegative, row sums ≤ 0, T nonsingular). Its Laplace–Stieltjes transform is f̃(s) = α(sI − T)^{-1}(−T)·1.

The order of a PH distribution is the smallest n for which it admits such a representation. A classical necessary condition (O'Cinneide's eigenvalue/angle condition) on the eigenvalues of T provides, for any given PH distribution, a lower bound n_min on the order of any phase-type representation of it.

Consider the family of PH distributions whose Laplace transforms have the form
   f̃(s) = 1 / q(s),    q(s) = (1 + s/c)(1 + s/(a+ib))(1 + s/(a−ib)),
with parameters a, b, c > 0 (so q has one real pole −c and a complex-conjugate pair of poles −a ± ib), under the assumption that f̃ is indeed the Laplace transform of some PH distribution. Let n_min denote the lower bound on the order coming from the eigenvalue/angle condition applied to such a distribution.

Question: Does every such PH distribution admit a phase-type representation of order exactly n_min?

No source found that conclusively confirms or refutes the specific conjecture that the eigenvalue/angle lower bound n_min is always attainable in the one-real-pole plus one-complex-pair case. Status appears unresolved.

paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
original_question: How is cyclicity in the directed graph of a phase-type representation related to the occurrence of non-real poles in the Laplace transform of the associated phase-type distribution? Characterize when cyclicity is compulsory, when a distribution with real poles can nevertheless have a natural or smaller cyclic representation, and whether cyclic representations can have smaller order than every acyclic representation of the same distribution.
self_contained_problem:
A phase-type distribution is the distribution of the absorption time of a continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space {1,...,n,n+1}, where state n+1 is absorbing and states 1,...,n are transient. Such a distribution is specified by a pair (α, A), called a phase-type representation, where α is a row sub-stochastic probability vector on {1,...,n} (the initial distribution on the transient states) and A is an n×n subgenerator matrix (off-diagonal entries nonnegative, row sums ≤ 0, and A nonsingular). The density is f(t) = α e^{At}(-A)·1 for t ≥ 0, and the Laplace transform is α(sI − A)^{-1}(-A)·1, a rational function whose poles are eigenvalues of A.

To a representation (α, A) one associates its directed graph G(α,A) on vertices {1,...,n,n+1}, with an arc i → j (i ≠ j, i,j ∈ {1,...,n}) whenever A_{ij} > 0, and an arc i → n+1 whenever (-A·1)_i > 0. The representation is called acyclic if G(α,A) has no directed cycle among the transient states, and cyclic otherwise. The order of a representation is its number n of transient states; the order of a phase-type distribution F is the minimum order over all representations of F.

Investigate the following questions:

(a) Characterize precisely the phase-type distributions F for which every phase-type representation is cyclic (i.e., cyclicity is compulsory). In particular, prove or disprove: a phase-type distribution F admits an acyclic representation if and only if the Laplace transform of F has only real poles.

(b) Suppose F has only real poles (so an acyclic representation exists). Determine when F nevertheless admits a "natural" cyclic representation of order no larger than (or strictly smaller than) the minimum acyclic order, and give a constructive characterization of such cases.

(c) Decide whether there exists a phase-type distribution F all of whose cyclic representations have strictly smaller order than every acyclic representation of F, and characterize the class of such distributions.
status_search_result: The relationship between cyclicity of a phase-type representation and non-real poles of the Laplace transform is acknowledged as not fully understood in the literature. It is known that if the Laplace transform has only real poles, an acyclic representation exists; the monocyclic / bidiagonal representations of Mocanu–Commault provide canonical cyclic forms. However, a complete characterization of when cyclicity is compulsory, when cyclic representations beat acyclic ones in order, and the general minimal-order question remain open problems.

paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
original_question: Determine whether the examples in Figures 1 and 2 are truly minimal. More precisely, prove or disprove that the smallest graph with at least two interlacing values for exponential subgraph centrality has 9 vertices, and that the smallest graph with at least two interlacing values for resolvent centrality has 10 vertices.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple, undirected, connected graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A$. For a parameter $\beta>0$, define the exponential subgraph centrality of vertex $i$ as
$$ SC_{\exp}(i;\beta) = [e^{\beta A}]_{ii}, $$
and, for $0<\alpha<1/\rho(A)$ (where $\rho(A)$ is the spectral radius of $A$), the resolvent subgraph centrality of vertex $i$ as
$$ SC_{\mathrm{res}}(i;\alpha) = [(I-\alpha A)^{-1}]_{ii}. $$
For two distinct vertices $i,j$, call a positive value of the parameter an interlacing value if the centralities of $i$ and $j$ are equal at that parameter while their ordering reverses on either side of it; equivalently, the function $\beta\mapsto SC_{\exp}(i;\beta)-SC_{\exp}(j;\beta)$ (respectively $\alpha\mapsto SC_{\mathrm{res}}(i;\alpha)-SC_{\mathrm{res}}(j;\alpha)$) vanishes and changes sign at that value. Say that $G$ has at least two interlacing values for exponential (respectively resolvent) subgraph centrality if there exists a pair of vertices for which the corresponding difference function has at least two positive sign-changing zeros.

Prove or disprove:

paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
context_brief: Comparing resolvent and subgraph interlacing counts
original_question: For a graph G with adjacency matrix A and spectral radius ρ, the resolvent centrality of vertex i is RC(i, α) = [(I − αA)^{-1}]_{ii} for 0 < α < 1/ρ. For a fixed pair of vertices, compare the numbers of interlacing values for resolvent centrality and exponential subgraph centrality. Is it always true that the number of α for which RC(i, α) = RC(j, α) is less than or equal to the number of β for which [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}? Prove or disprove this statement.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$ and spectral radius $\rho = \rho(A)$. For a vertex $i$ of $G$ and a real parameter $\alpha$ with $0 < \alpha < 1/\rho$, define the resolvent (subgraph) centrality of $i$ by
$$RC(i,\alpha) = \bigl[(I - \alpha A)^{-1}\bigr]_{ii},$$
and for a real parameter $\beta > 0$ define the exponential subgraph centrality of $i$ by
$$SC(i,\beta) = \bigl[e^{\beta A}\bigr]_{ii}.$$
For a fixed pair of distinct vertices $i,j$ of $G$, call a value of the parameter an "interlacing value" for the respective centrality if the centralities of $i$ and $j$ coincide there: i.e. an $\alpha \in (0, 1/\rho)$ with $RC(i,\alpha) = RC(j,\alpha)$, or a $\beta > 0$ with $SC(i,\beta) = SC(j,\beta)$.

Let $N_{RC}(i,j)$ denote the number of interlacing values of $\alpha \in (0, 1/\rho)$ for the resolvent centrality and let $N_{SC}(i,j)$ denote the number of interlacing values of $\beta > 0$ for the exponential subgraph centrality.

Prove or disprove: for every graph $G$ and every pair of distinct vertices $i,j$,
$$N_{RC}(i,j) \;\le\; N_{SC}(i,j).$$
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in the work introducing it, and a search does not reveal any subsequent publication resolving the inequality between the counts of interlacing values for resolvent centrality and exponential subgraph centrality for general graphs. No proof or counterexample has been located.

paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
original_question: Let E^2 denote the Euclidean plane. A set X is monochromatic in a coloring if all points of a congruent copy of X receive the same color. For every non-equilateral triangle T, viewed as the set of its three vertices, must every 2-coloring of E^2 contain a monochromatic congruent copy of T?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{E}^2$ denote the Euclidean plane. Given a finite set $X \subset \mathbb{E}^2$ and a coloring $c: \mathbb{E}^2 \to \{1,2\}$, say that $X$ is monochromatic (under $c$) if there exists a congruent copy $X'$ of $X$ in $\mathbb{E}^2$ such that all points of $X'$ receive the same color. A triangle $T$ is identified with the 3-point set of its vertices, and is called non-equilateral if its three side lengths are not all equal.

Prove or disprove: for every non-equilateral triangle $T \subset \mathbb{E}^2$ and every 2-coloring $c : \mathbb{E}^2 \to \{1,2\}$, there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.
status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus) remains open in general. It has been verified for several special families of triangles (e.g., right triangles, isosceles triangles with specific ratios, and—established more recently—all 3-term arithmetic progressions, i.e., degenerate triangles whose vertices are collinear and equally spaced). No counterexample is known, but a complete proof for arbitrary non-equilateral triangles has not been established.

paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
context_brief: Triangles in three-space with three colors
original_question: For every triangle T, must every 3-coloring of Euclidean three-space E^3 contain a monochromatic congruent copy of T?
self_contained_problem:
Let $E^3$ denote three-dimensional Euclidean space. A coloring of $E^3$ with $r$ colors is a function $\chi: E^3 \to \{1, 2, \dots, r\}$. Given a finite point configuration $T \subset E^3$, we say a coloring $\chi$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$ if there exists an isometry $\sigma$ of $E^3$ such that $\chi$ is constant on $\sigma(T)$. Write $E^3 \to_r T$ to mean that every $r$-coloring of $E^3$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.

Prove or disprove: for every (nondegenerate) triangle $T$ (i.e., every set of three non-collinear points in the plane, considered up to congruence), one has $E^3 \to_3 T$; that is, every $3$-coloring of $E^3$ contains three points forming a triangle congruent to $T$ all of the same color.
status_search_result: The conjecture that every 3-coloring of $E^3$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of any given triangle is a well-known open problem in Euclidean Ramsey theory, stated as a conjecture in surveys of open problems by Graham and collaborators. No proof or counterexample appears in the literature; only special cases and related planar/two-color statements have been studied.

paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
original_question: For each dimension n, determine the chromatic number χ(E^n), the least number of colors needed to color Euclidean n-space so that no two points at unit distance have the same color. In particular, determine χ(E^2), where the source records the classical bounds 4 ≤ χ(E^2) ≤ 7, and χ(E^3), where it records 6 ≤ χ(E^3) ≤ 15.
self_contained_problem:
For each integer n ≥ 2, let E^n denote n-dimensional Euclidean space. Define the chromatic number χ(E^n) to be the least cardinal k such that there exists a function c : E^n → {1, 2, …, k} (a "coloring") with the property that c(x) ≠ c(y) whenever x, y ∈ E^n satisfy ‖x − y‖ = 1.

Determine χ(E^n) for each n ≥ 2. In particular:

(a) Determine χ(E^2). It is classical that 4 ≤ χ(E^2) ≤ 7; pin down the exact value.

(b) Determine χ(E^3). It is known that 6 ≤ χ(E^3) ≤ 15; pin down the exact value.
status_search_result: The Hadwiger–Nelson problem remains open. The lower bound for χ(E^2) was improved from 4 to 5 by de Grey in 2018 (and subsequent work has reduced the size of 5-chromatic unit-distance graphs), while the upper bound of 7 from 1950 has not been improved. Current best bounds are 5 ≤ χ(E^2) ≤ 7. Higher-dimensional cases, including n = 3, also remain unresolved, with active work continuing in 2024–2025.

paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
original_question: Is every four-point subset of a circle Ramsey, meaning that for every number of colors r, all sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean spaces colored with r colors must contain a monochromatic congruent copy of that four-point circular set?
self_contained_problem:
A finite set $K \subset \mathbb{R}^k$ is called Ramsey if for every positive integer $r$ there exists $n = n(K,r)$ such that for every coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $r$ colors, there is a monochromatic subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is congruent (i.e., isometric via a Euclidean isometry of $\mathbb{R}^n$) to $K$.

Prove or disprove: every 4-point subset of a circle in the plane is Ramsey. Equivalently, for every set $K = \{p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4\}$ of four points lying on a common circle, and for every positive integer $r$, there exists $n$ such that any $r$-coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $K$.
status_search_result: The conjecture that every 4-point subset of a circle is Ramsey remains open in general. Křiž proved it in the special case where the four points form a trapezoid (a pair of opposite sides parallel). General 4-point cyclic sets are typically not subtransitive, and existing techniques (transitive/solvable symmetry groups, non-sphericality) do not apply, leaving the full conjecture unresolved as of recent surveys and REU/expository papers.

paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
original_question: A finite set X is sphere-Ramsey if, for every number of colors r, there exist a dimension N and a radius ρ such that every r-coloring of the sphere S^N(ρ) contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X. If X is Ramsey in Euclidean space, must X also be sphere-Ramsey?

For a finite set X ⊂ ℝ^n and a positive integer r, say that X is Ramsey if there exists a positive integer N such that every r-coloring of ℝ^N contains a monochromatic subset congruent to X. Say that X is sphere-Ramsey if for every positive integer r there exist a positive integer N and a positive real number ρ such that every r-coloring of the sphere S^N(ρ) = {x ∈ ℝ^{N+1} : |x| = ρ} contains a monochromatic subset congruent to X.

Prove or disprove: every finite Ramsey set X ⊂ ℝ^n is sphere-Ramsey.

paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
original_question: Characterize all finite line-segment configurations E that are edge-Ramsey: those for which, for every number of colors r, every sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space has the property that any r-coloring of its line segments contains a monochromatic copy of E.
self_contained_problem:
A line segment in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is an unordered pair of distinct points $\{x,y\} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. Two finite sets of line segments in Euclidean spaces are called congruent copies of each other if one can be mapped to the other by a Euclidean isometry (preserving the segment structure).

Let $E$ be a finite configuration of line segments in some Euclidean space. Say that $E$ is edge-Ramsey if for every positive integer $r$ there exists an integer $N=N(E,r)$ such that, for every $n \ge N$, every coloring of the set of all line segments of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $r$ colors contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $E$ (i.e., a congruent copy of $E$ all of whose segments receive the same color).

Problem: Give a complete characterization of the finite line-segment configurations $E$ that are edge-Ramsey.
status_search_result: Surveys and recent expository works on Euclidean Ramsey theory list the characterization of edge-Ramsey configurations as a long-standing open problem. Only partial results are known: regular n-gons are edge-Ramsey for n=2,3,4, while the general classification remains unresolved, and no widely accepted conjectural characterization has been proposed.

original_question: For every integer n, must every set of 2^(n-2)+1 points in the plane in general position, meaning no three points are collinear, contain n points that are the vertices of a convex n-gon?
self_contained_problem:
A finite set of points in the Euclidean plane is said to be in general position if no three of its points are collinear. A set of n points is said to form a convex n-gon if the points are the vertices of a convex polygon (equivalently, none of the points lies in the convex hull of the others).

Prove or disprove the following: for every integer n ≥ 3, every set of 2^(n−2) + 1 points in the plane in general position contains n points that are the vertices of a convex n-gon.

paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
original_question: Let N be the set of natural numbers. If A is a subset of N and the reciprocal sum Σ_{a in A} 1/a diverges, must A contain arithmetic progressions of every finite length? The source also notes that it was not even known whether this hypothesis forces a 3-term arithmetic progression.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$ denote the set of positive integers. A finite arithmetic progression of length $k$ is a set of the form $\{a, a+d, a+2d, \dots, a+(k-1)d\}$ with $a\in\mathbb{N}$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$.

Prove or disprove: For every subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ satisfying
$$\sum_{a\in A}\frac{1}{a}=\infty,$$
and for every integer $k\geq 3$, the set $A$ contains an arithmetic progression of length $k$.

(The special case $k=3$ asks whether divergence of the reciprocal sum already forces the existence of three distinct elements $a,b,c\in A$ with $b-a=c-b>0$.)

paper_title: Fluctuation Limit of Branching Processes with Immigration and Estimation of the Means
context_brief: Estimator normalization in degenerate variance regime
original_question: Consider a triangular sequence of Galton-Watson branching processes with immigration X_k^(n), started from X_0^(n)=0, where m_n = 1 + alpha/n + o(1/n), sigma_n^2 = beta/n + o(1/n), lambda_n tends to lambda > 0, and b_n^2 tends to b^2. Let the conditional least-squares estimator of m_n be formed from the regression X_k^(n)=m_n X_{k-1}^(n)+lambda_n+M_k^(n) when lambda_n is known, and let the joint conditional least-squares estimators estimate (m_n, lambda_n) when both means are unknown. In the fully degenerate variance regime beta=0 and b^2=0, the normal limits obtained with the norming factors n^{3/2} for the m_n estimators and n^{1/2} for the lambda_n estimator collapse to point masses. What replacement normalization and limiting distribution, if any, describe these least-squares estimators in that degenerate regime?
self_contained_problem:
For each integer n ≥ 1, let (X_k^{(n)})_{k ≥ 0} be a Galton–Watson branching process with immigration, defined on a common probability space, with X_0^{(n)} = 0 and the recursion

  X_k^{(n)} = sum_{j=1}^{X_{k-1}^{(n)}} ξ_{k,j}^{(n)} + ε_k^{(n)},  k = 1, 2, …,

where, for each n, {ξ_{k,j}^{(n)} : k, j ≥ 1} are i.i.d. nonnegative integer-valued offspring random variables with mean m_n = E ξ_{1,1}^{(n)} and variance σ_n^2 = Var ξ_{1,1}^{(n)}, and {ε_k^{(n)} : k ≥ 1} are i.i.d. nonnegative integer-valued immigration random variables, independent of the offspring variables, with mean λ_n = E ε_1^{(n)} and variance b_n^2 = Var ε_1^{(n)}. Assume the nearly critical regime

  m_n = 1 + α/n + o(1/n),  σ_n^2 = β/n + o(1/n),  λ_n → λ > 0,  b_n^2 → b^2,

as n → ∞, with α ∈ ℝ and β, b^2 ≥ 0.

Writing the regression form X_k^{(n)} = m_n X_{k-1}^{(n)} + λ_n + M_k^{(n)} with martingale differences M_k^{(n)}, define for a sample of size n:
 • the conditional least-squares estimator m̃_n of m_n when λ_n is known,
 • the joint conditional least-squares estimators (m̂_n, λ̂_n) of (m_n, λ_n) when both means are unknown.

In the nondegenerate case (β > 0 or b^2 > 0) it is known that n^{3/2}(m̃_n − m_n), n^{3/2}(m̂_n − m_n), and n^{1/2}(λ̂_n − λ_n) converge in distribution to nondegenerate normal laws. In the fully degenerate variance regime β = 0 and b^2 = 0, however, these normalized quantities converge in probability to 0, so the factors n^{3/2} and n^{1/2} are not the correct rates.

Determine the appropriate norming sequences a_n, a'_n, c_n and identify the (necessarily nondegenerate) limiting distributions, if they exist, of

  a_n (m̃_n − m_n),  a'_n (m̂_n − m_n),  c_n (λ̂_n − λ_n),

as n → ∞ under the degenerate regime β = 0, b^2 = 0.

The status of this specific question could not be conclusively verified.

paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
original_question: In ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems, does the observed exchange bias originate directly from ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic interfacial coupling, or does it require some other interfacial magnetic state?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterostructure formed by stacking a two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnet (FM) on top of a two-dimensional van der Waals antiferromagnet (AFM), with an atomically sharp interface between them. After field-cooling such a bilayer below the Néel temperature of the AFM and the Curie temperature of the FM, the hysteresis loop of the FM layer is typically observed to be shifted along the magnetic-field axis; this shift is the exchange bias (EB) field H_EB.

Determine the microscopic origin of the exchange bias in such FM/AFM van der Waals systems. Specifically, decide between the following two alternatives (and justify the answer with a quantitative model that predicts H_EB as a function of interfacial exchange coupling, AFM anisotropy, layer thicknesses, and temperature):

(a) The exchange bias arises directly from the interfacial exchange coupling between the ordered FM moments and the uncompensated/compensated AFM moments at the interface, i.e. a direct FM/AFM interfacial coupling fully accounts for the measured H_EB.

(b) The exchange bias cannot be accounted for by a direct FM/AFM interfacial coupling alone, and instead requires the presence of an additional interfacial magnetic state (for example a frozen spin-glass-like layer, a canted or reconstructed interface phase, a proximity-induced magnetic layer, or interfacial defect-stabilized moments) that mediates or generates the bias.

Provide a theoretical framework or experimental criterion that distinguishes (a) from (b) in two-dimensional van der Waals FM/AFM heterostructures.

original_question: How does the type of antiferromagnetic ordering in the antiferromagnetic layer affect exchange-bias behavior in ferromagnet/antiferromagnet van der Waals systems?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a magnetic heterostructure consisting of a two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnetic (FM) layer placed in contact with a two-dimensional van der Waals antiferromagnetic (AFM) layer. The exchange-bias (EB) effect refers to a horizontal shift H_E of the FM hysteresis loop along the magnetic-field axis after the heterostructure is field-cooled through the Néel temperature of the AFM layer; this shift originates from the interfacial exchange coupling between uncompensated AFM moments and the FM magnetization.

Antiferromagnetic order in a van der Waals layered material can take several distinct forms, including: 
(a) A-type ordering (ferromagnetic intralayer alignment with antiferromagnetic interlayer stacking), 
(b) C-type ordering (antiferromagnetic intralayer chains with ferromagnetic interlayer stacking), 
(c) G-type ordering (antiferromagnetic alignment with all nearest neighbors), 
(d) zigzag, stripy, or Néel intralayer orderings on the honeycomb lattice, 
(e) noncollinear or helical orderings.

1. Derive, from a microscopic spin Hamiltonian for the FM/AFM interface (including Heisenberg exchange, single-ion anisotropy, and interfacial coupling J_int), the dependence of the exchange-bias field H_E, the coercivity enhancement ΔH_c, and the blocking temperature T_B on the AFM ordering type listed above.

2. In particular, predict (i) for which ordering types H_E remains finite down to the monolayer or bilayer AFM limit, (ii) how the sign of H_E depends on the parity of AFM layers for A-type ordering, and (iii) how intralayer compensated versus uncompensated interfaces (as determined by the ordering type and crystallographic termination) modify the magnitude of H_E.

3. Provide a criterion, in terms of the AFM ordering wavevector and the FM/AFM lattice mismatch, that determines whether a robust exchange-bias effect can be observed.

Consider a two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructure consisting of a ferromagnetic (FM) layer stacked on an antiferromagnetic (AFM) layer, modeled by a layered Heisenberg-type spin Hamiltonian in which interlayer exchange couplings across the interface may be inhomogeneous (frustrated, defective, or randomly signed). (b) If such a disordered interfacial phase exists, can it by itself produce a nonzero exchange bias field H_E ≠ 0 in the FM layer's hysteresis loop, independently of any long-range AFM order in the bulk of the antiferromagnetic layer?

original_question: Can exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic systems be tuned by external stimuli such as electric field or strain?
self_contained_problem: Consider a magnetic heterostructure formed by stacking two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic layers (for instance, a ferromagnet/antiferromagnet bilayer such as Fe3GeTe2/FePS3 or CrCl3/Fe3GeTe2). paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
original_question: In Fe3GeTe2/CrCl3 van der Waals heterostructures, is exchange bias caused purely by direct ferromagnet/antiferromagnet coupling, or is it altered by an interfacial oxide or spin-cluster layer, magnetic proximity between Fe3GeTe2 and CrCl3, and charge transfer across the interface?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a van der Waals magnetic heterostructure obtained by stacking a thin flake of the itinerant ferromagnet Fe₃GeTe₂ (FGT) on top of (or beneath) a thin flake of the layered antiferromagnet CrCl₃, where CrCl₃ has ferromagnetic intralayer order and antiferromagnetic interlayer order below its Néel temperature. After field-cooling such a heterostructure, the hysteresis loop of the FGT layer is shifted along the field axis by an amount H_EB ≠ 0, a phenomenon known as exchange bias (EB).

Identify the microscopic origin of this exchange bias by determining, in a quantitative and mechanism-resolving manner, the relative contributions of the following four candidate effects:

(a) Direct interfacial exchange coupling between the ferromagnetic FGT spins and the uncompensated antiferromagnetic CrCl₃ spins at the shared van der Waals interface, treated as the conventional ferromagnet/antiferromagnet pinning mechanism.

(b) The presence of an interfacial oxide (or otherwise disordered) phase at the FGT/CrCl₃ interface that behaves as a layer of magnetic "spin clusters," with CrCl₃ then acting as a secondary pinning layer for these clusters rather than directly for FGT.

(c) Magnetic proximity coupling, in which the electronic wavefunctions of FGT and CrCl₃ hybridize across the van der Waals gap and induce modifications of the magnetization profile (e.g., interfacial spin polarization, exchange splitting, and altered anisotropy) in both layers.

(d) Interfacial charge transfer between FGT and CrCl₃, which can renormalize the carrier density and exchange interactions in FGT (possibly enhancing its Curie temperature and magnetization) and thereby influence the exchange bias.

The problem is: starting from a microscopic model of the FGT/CrCl₃ interface (including the possibility of an interfacial oxide/spin-cluster layer, proximity-induced exchange, and charge redistribution), derive H_EB(T, t_FGT, t_CrCl₃, H_FC) as a function of temperature, layer thicknesses, and cooling field, and decompose it into the contributions of mechanisms (a)–(d); equivalently, determine whether the observed exchange bias in FGT/CrCl₃ heterostructures is due purely to mechanism (a) or whether mechanisms (b), (c), and/or (d) make essential contributions.
category_tag: van der Waals magnetic heterostructures / exchange bias
status_search_result: Recent literature indicates that the microscopic mechanism of exchange bias in Fe3GeTe2/CrCl3 (and related FGT-based) heterostructures remains unresolved. Subsequent works have shown that surface oxidation of Fe3GeTe2 alone produces exchange bias via an antiferromagnetic surface oxide, and studies on CrPS4/Fe3GeTe2 explicitly invoke interfacial-oxide modulation; magnetic proximity and charge-transfer contributions are acknowledged but not quantitatively disentangled. No definitive decomposition of the four contributions has been established.

original_question: Do the exchange-bias and quantum anomalous Hall effects predicted for CrI3/MnBi2Te4 ferromagnet/antiferromagnet heterostructures occur experimentally, and can analogous exchange-bias and quantum anomalous Hall phenomena be realized by interfacing MnBi2Te4 or related topological antiferromagnets with other van der Waals ferromagnets such as Fe3GeTe2 or Fe5GeTe2?

Consider van der Waals magnetic heterostructures formed by stacking the layered antiferromagnetic magnetic topological insulator MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ with two-dimensional ferromagnetic materials. First-principles calculations for the ferromagnet/antiferromagnet heterostructure CrI$_3$/MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ predict (i) a sizable exchange-bias field at the interface, arising from hybridization between the Cr $e_g$ orbitals and Te $p$ orbitals, and (ii) the stabilization of out-of-plane surface magnetization that drives a zero-field quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) phase in MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ thin films.

Address the following:

(a) Can both the predicted exchange-bias effect and the predicted zero-field quantum anomalous Hall effect in CrI$_3$/MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ heterostructures be confirmed by direct experimental measurements (e.g., magnetotransport, magneto-optical Kerr effect)?

(b) Replacing CrI$_3$ with another two-dimensional ferromagnet such as Fe$_3$GeTe$_2$ or Fe$_5$GeTe$_2$ (or interfacing related intrinsic antiferromagnetic topological insulators in place of MnBi$_2$Te$_4$), can analogous exchange-bias phenomena and a QAH state be experimentally realized in such heterostructures, and characterize the magnitude of the exchange bias, its temperature dependence, and the conditions (thickness, gating, temperature) under which QAH transport emerges.
status_search_result: Exchange bias has been experimentally observed in MnBi2Te4-based van der Waals heterostructures, including a 2024 report of exchange bias in MnBi2Te4/Fe3GeTe2 (Applied Physics Letters) and intrinsic exchange-biased anomalous Hall effect within MnBi2Te4 itself (Nature Communications 2024). However, an unambiguous experimental demonstration of the zero-field quantum anomalous Hall effect in CrI3/MnBi2Te4 or Fe(3,5)GeTe2/MnBi2Te4 heterostructures has not been clearly established, so the QAH portion of the question remains open while the exchange-bias portion is partially confirmed.

original_question: In Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 and related van der Waals spin-valve structures, what microscopic mechanism causes the magnetoresistance enhancement, is the magnetoresistance asymmetry caused by oxidized Fe3GeTe2 surface layers, and how do magnetic proximity, magnetic-domain reconstruction, spin-orbit coupling proximity, and charge transfer across the Fe3GeTe2/MoS2 interface contribute to the observed transport behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Consider vertical van der Waals spin-valve heterostructures of the form Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 (and closely related structures in which a monolayer or few-layer MoS2 spacer is sandwiched between two Fe3GeTe2 ferromagnetic electrodes). In such devices, current is driven perpendicular to the layers and the magnetoresistance (MR) is measured as a function of an external magnetic field that switches the two Fe3GeTe2 layers between parallel and antiparallel configurations. Experimentally, the MR is found to be substantially larger than in analogous spin valves with conventional ferromagnetic electrodes, and the MR versus field curves frequently exhibit an asymmetry with respect to field reversal. The outermost atomic layers of Fe3GeTe2 are prone to oxidation, and the oxidized surface layer may couple antiferromagnetically to the interior Fe3GeTe2. The MoS2 monolayer has strong spin–orbit coupling and a band structure that can be modified by proximity to a ferromagnet, and substantial interfacial charge transfer can occur between Fe3GeTe2 and MoS2.

Determine the following:
(a) The microscopic mechanism responsible for the magnetoresistance enhancement observed in such Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 spin valves relative to spin valves with conventional ferromagnetic electrodes.
(b) Whether the asymmetry observed in the MR versus field curves originates from an oxidized Fe3GeTe2 surface layer that is antiferromagnetically coupled to the underlying Fe3GeTe2 interior.
(c) The respective quantitative contributions of (i) magnetic proximity-induced magnetization of the MoS2 spacer, (ii) reconstruction of magnetic domains in Fe3GeTe2 near the interface, (iii) spin–orbit coupling proximity effects transferred from MoS2 into Fe3GeTe2, and (iv) interfacial charge transfer across the Fe3GeTe2/MoS2 interface, to the measured spin-dependent transport.

Provide a theoretical and/or experimental framework that disentangles these contributions and either confirms or refutes each proposed mechanism.
status_search_result: Recent works have reported related observations and partial mechanisms: an SOC proximity effect in MoS2/Fe3GeTe2 has been demonstrated (Applied Physics Letters, 2022), proximity-induced MR enhancement has been identified in the analogous Fe3GeTe2/NbSe2/Fe3GeTe2 junction (ACS AMI, 2023), and large tunable MR has been reported in van der Waals FM/semiconductor junctions (Nat. Commun., 2023). However, no single study has jointly disentangled the relative contributions of magnetic proximity, domain reconstruction, SOC proximity, and charge transfer in Fe3GeTe2/MoS2/Fe3GeTe2, nor conclusively attributed the MR asymmetry to oxidized surface Fe3GeTe2 layers. The full question therefore remains open.

paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
original_question: Can ferromagnet/ferromagnet coupling at a defective van der Waals VSe2/MoS2 interface generate an exchange-bias effect even though the interface is not a conventional ferromagnet/antiferromagnet interface?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a van der Waals heterostructure formed by a monolayer of VSe2 (a transition-metal dichalcogenide that, in monolayer form, exhibits ferromagnetic ordering attributed to defects and edge states) deposited on a single crystal of MoS2 (another transition-metal dichalcogenide whose pristine bulk form is nonmagnetic but which, with defects, can host localized magnetic moments behaving as a weak ferromagnet). In conventional exchange-bias (EB) systems, a horizontal shift of the magnetic hysteresis loop along the applied-field axis arises at an interface between a ferromagnet (FM) and an antiferromagnet (AFM) after field cooling, due to unidirectional anisotropy imprinted by the pinned AFM moments on the FM. The VSe2/MoS2 interface, however, is nominally an FM/FM interface (both layers being defect-induced ferromagnets) rather than an FM/AFM interface.

Question: Can the interfacial exchange coupling between two defect-induced ferromagnets at a van der Waals VSe2/MoS2 interface produce a genuine exchange-bias effect (i.e., a measurable horizontal shift of the field-cooled hysteresis loop), despite the absence of a conventional antiferromagnetic pinning layer? Equivalently, determine whether FM/FM coupling at such a defective vdW interface is a viable mechanism for exchange bias, and if so characterize the conditions (defect density, interfacial coupling strength, anisotropy, temperature) under which a finite EB field is expected.
category_tag: Exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic heterostructures

original_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field K, and let D1 be an admissible subcategory of Db(X1) and D2 an admissible subcategory of Db(X2). Must every exact fully faithful functor F: D1 -> D2 be of Fourier-Mukai type?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field and let $X_1, X_2$ be smooth projective varieties over $K$. Denote by $D^b(X_i)$ the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X_i$. Recall that a full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal{D} \subset D^b(X)$ is called admissible if the inclusion functor admits both a left and a right adjoint. An exact functor $F\colon \mathcal{D}_1 \to \mathcal{D}_2$ between triangulated subcategories $\mathcal{D}_i \subset D^b(X_i)$ is said to be of Fourier–Mukai type if there exists an object $E \in D^b(X_1 \times_K X_2)$ such that $F$ is isomorphic to the restriction to $\mathcal{D}_1$ of the functor
$$\Phi_E(-) := R(p_2)_*\bigl(E \otimes^L p_1^*(-)\bigr)\colon D^b(X_1) \to D^b(X_2),$$
where $p_1, p_2$ denote the two projections from $X_1 \times_K X_2$.

Question: Let $\mathcal{D}_1 \subset D^b(X_1)$ and $\mathcal{D}_2 \subset D^b(X_2)$ be admissible subcategories. Must every exact fully faithful functor $F\colon \mathcal{D}_1 \to \mathcal{D}_2$ be of Fourier–Mukai type?
status_search_result: The question of whether every exact fully faithful functor between admissible subcategories of bounded derived categories of smooth projective varieties is of Fourier–Mukai type generalizes Orlov's representability theorem. Surveys and recent work by Canonaco–Stellari describe this as an open problem; Orlov's theorem covers the case where the source is the full $D^b(X_1)$, but the admissible-subcategory version is not known in general.

original_question: The derived Torelli theorem for Enriques surfaces says that if X1 and X2 are smooth projective surfaces over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2, X1 is an Enriques surface, and Db(X1) is equivalent to Db(X2), then X1 is isomorphic to X2. Does this theorem remain true in characteristic 2 for some or all of the three characteristic-2 families of Enriques surfaces: classical, singular, and supersingular Enriques surfaces?
status_search_result: A 2016 note by Honigs-Lombardi-Tirabassi shows that the (twisted) derived category can distinguish the three families of Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2, but this does not establish the full derived Torelli statement. Subsequent refined derived Torelli results (Saccà–Macrì and others, 2019–2021) explicitly assume characteristic different from 2. No source found that proves or disproves derived Torelli for any of the three characteristic-2 families, so the question appears to remain open.

original_question: Let X be an Enriques surface and let Ku(X, L) be the Kuznetsov component determined by a collection L of exceptional line bundles in a semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X) = <Ku(X, L), L>. Is Ku(X, L) indecomposable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $D^b(X)$ denote its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves. Suppose $\mathcal{L} = (L_1, \ldots, L_n)$ is an exceptional collection of line bundles on $X$ (i.e., each $L_i$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ext}^k(L_i,L_i) = 0$ for $k \neq 0$ and $\mathrm{Ext}^k(L_i,L_j) = 0$ for $i > j$ and all $k$) such that there is a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathrm{Ku}(X, \mathcal{L}),\, L_1, \ldots, L_n \rangle,$$
where $\mathrm{Ku}(X, \mathcal{L})$ — the Kuznetsov component — is the right orthogonal to $\langle L_1, \ldots, L_n \rangle$ in $D^b(X)$.

Determine whether $\mathrm{Ku}(X, \mathcal{L})$ is always indecomposable as a triangulated category, i.e., whether it admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition.
status_search_result: A 2022 survey on categorical Torelli theorems lists this exact question as an open problem (Question 3.9(ii)), noting that a positive answer would yield a counterexample to the Jordan–Hölder property for semiorthogonal decompositions and would have implications for the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on Ku(X,L). No resolution is reported in the available literature.

original_question: If X is a cubic threefold and Ku(X) is the Kuznetsov component appearing in the standard semiorthogonal decomposition of Db(X), is Ku(X) indecomposable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth cubic threefold, and let $D^b(X)$ denote the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X$. Let $H$ denote the hyperplane class. There is a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathrm{Ku}(X),\, \mathcal{O}_X,\, \mathcal{O}_X(H) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component is defined by
$$\mathrm{Ku}(X) = \{ E \in D^b(X) : \mathrm{Hom}^\bullet(\mathcal{O}_X, E) = 0 = \mathrm{Hom}^\bullet(\mathcal{O}_X(H), E)\}.$$
A $\mathbb{C}$-linear triangulated category $\mathcal{T}$ is said to be (semiorthogonally) indecomposable if it admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition $\mathcal{T} = \langle \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B} \rangle$ with both $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ nonzero admissible subcategories.

Question: Is the Kuznetsov component $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ indecomposable for every smooth cubic threefold $X$?
status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive proof or disproof of the indecomposability of the Kuznetsov component of a smooth cubic threefold. The Kuznetsov component is widely studied (stability conditions, categorical Torelli, moduli spaces), but indecomposability in the sense of admitting no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition does not appear to have a published resolution in the sources surveyed; the question appears to remain open.

context_brief: Bogomolov inequality for a P^6 complete intersection
original_question: Let X be a Calabi-Yau threefold given as a complete intersection of one cubic hypersurface and two quadric hypersurfaces in P^6. Is it possible to prove a stronger Bogomolov inequality for slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves on X, analogous to the inequalities proved in the cited quintic and quadric-quartic cases, in a way that implies inequality (4.5)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^6$ be a smooth Calabi–Yau threefold obtained as the complete intersection of one cubic hypersurface and two quadric hypersurfaces, and let $H$ denote the restriction of the hyperplane class of $\mathbb{P}^6$ to $X$. For a torsion-free coherent sheaf $E$ on $X$, write $\mathrm{ch}^s(E) = e^{-sH}\,\mathrm{ch}(E)$ for the twisted Chern character with twist parameter $s \in \mathbb{R}$, and set
$$\Delta_H(E) = (H^2\,\mathrm{ch}_1(E))^2 - 2\,(H^3\,\mathrm{ch}_0(E))(H\,\mathrm{ch}_2(E)).$$
For real parameters $q,s$ with $q > s^2/2$, consider the inequality
$$(2q - s^2)\,\Delta_H(E) \;+\; 4\,(H\,\mathrm{ch}^{\,s}_2(E))^2 \;-\; 6\,H^2\,\mathrm{ch}^{\,s}_1(E)\cdot \mathrm{ch}^{\,s}_3(E) \;\ge\; 0. \qquad (\star)$$

Prove (or disprove) a strengthened Bogomolov–Gieseker type inequality for $H$-slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves on $X$ — in the spirit of the strengthened inequalities established for the smooth quintic threefold in $\mathbb{P}^4$ and for the complete intersection of a quadric and a quartic in $\mathbb{P}^5$ — that is strong enough to imply $(\star)$ for all tilt-semistable objects on $X$ in the relevant parameter range, thereby yielding the construction of Bridgeland stability conditions on $D^b(X)$.
status_search_result: Strengthened Bogomolov–Gieseker inequalities of this type were previously known for the quintic threefold and for the (2,4) complete intersection in P^5. A 2025 preprint reduces the BMT/Γ-BMT conjecture for complete intersection Calabi–Yau threefolds in (weighted) projective space with Picard rank one to a Brill–Noether-type inequality on hyperplane curves and claims the inequality for a broad class of CICYs including those in projective space generated by a very ample H; the (2,2,3) complete intersection in P^6 fits in this class, although it is not enumerated explicitly. Hence the problem appears at least partially resolved, with no widely cited direct verification of (4.5) specific to X_{2,2,3} found.

context_brief: Alternative proof strategy for cubic-threefold Torelli
original_question: Can the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds, namely Theorem 5.4, be proved by using the extension techniques for Fourier-Mukai equivalences that are discussed in Section 3.1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth cubic threefold. The bounded derived category $\mathrm{D}^b(Y)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$\mathrm{D}^b(Y) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(Y), \mathcal{O}_Y, \mathcal{O}_Y(1) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(Y)$ is defined as the right orthogonal of $\langle \mathcal{O}_Y, \mathcal{O}_Y(1)\rangle$. The categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds asserts that for two smooth complex cubic threefolds $Y$ and $Y'$, an equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(Y) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(Y')$ of $\mathbb{C}$-linear triangulated categories (of Fourier–Mukai type) implies that $Y \cong Y'$ as projective varieties.

A general "extension technique" for Fourier–Mukai equivalences provides criteria under which an exact equivalence $\Phi : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{A}'$ between admissible subcategories $\mathcal{A} \subset \mathrm{D}^b(X)$ and $\mathcal{A}' \subset \mathrm{D}^b(X')$ appearing in semiorthogonal decompositions can be lifted to an equivalence $\widetilde{\Phi} : \mathrm{D}^b(X) \to \mathrm{D}^b(X')$ of the ambient derived categories.

Problem. Using only such extension techniques for Fourier–Mukai equivalences (i.e. extending a given equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(Y) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(Y')$ to an equivalence $\mathrm{D}^b(Y) \simeq \mathrm{D}^b(Y')$ and then invoking Bondal–Orlov reconstruction), give a proof of the categorical Torelli theorem for smooth complex cubic threefolds.
status_search_result: A 2023/2024 paper by Z. Liu, "On Fourier–Mukai type autoequivalences of Kuznetsov components of cubic threefolds" (Math. Nachr., 2024), provides an alternative proof of the Fourier–Mukai version of the categorical Torelli theorem for smooth complex cubic threefolds by extending Fourier–Mukai equivalences between Kuznetsov components to equivalences of the ambient derived categories, exactly along the lines requested. Subsequent work (e.g. on non-Eckardt cubic threefolds via equivariant Kuznetsov components) further develops this strategy.

original_question: Suppose D is an admissible subcategory of Db(X) that admits Serre-invariant stability conditions and has numerical Grothendieck group N(D) of rank 2. Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on D under the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth projective variety over the complex numbers, and let D^b(X) denote its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves. An admissible subcategory D ⊂ D^b(X) is a full triangulated subcategory whose inclusion admits both left and right adjoints; such a D has its own Serre functor S_D. A Bridgeland stability condition σ = (Z, A) on D (with respect to a fixed surjection from the numerical Grothendieck group N(D) to a finite-rank lattice) is called Serre-invariant if S_D · σ lies in the same orbit as σ under the natural action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(ℝ) on the space of stability conditions Stab(D).

Assume that D is an admissible subcategory of D^b(X) which admits at least one Serre-invariant stability condition, and that the numerical Grothendieck group N(D) has rank 2.

Question: Is the set of Serre-invariant stability conditions on D a single orbit under the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(ℝ)?
status_search_result: Uniqueness of the orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions has been established in several geometric cases of admissible subcategories with rank-2 numerical Grothendieck group — notably for Kuznetsov components of cubic threefolds (Feyzbakhsh–Pertusi), and subsequently for Kuznetsov components of del Pezzo threefolds of degree ≥ 2 and prime Fano threefolds of genus ≥ 6, under fractional Calabi–Yau hypotheses. A fully general answer for all admissible subcategories satisfying the stated hypotheses does not appear to be available in the literature; the question is partially solved in important cases but not settled in full generality.

context_brief: Serre-invariant stability on the Veronese double cone
original_question: Let Y1 be the prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1, equivalently the degree-6 hypersurface in the weighted projective space P(1,1,1,2,3) known as the Veronese double cone. Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on Ku(Y1) under the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Y_1$ denote the smooth prime Fano threefold of Picard rank one, index two, and degree one, equivalently realized as a smooth hypersurface of degree $6$ in the weighted projective space $\mathbb{P}(1,1,1,2,3)$ (the Veronese double cone). Let $\mathcal{D}^b(Y_1)$ be its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves, and let $\mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(H)$ denote the polarization corresponding to the ample generator $H$ of $\operatorname{Pic}(Y_1)$. Define the Kuznetsov component
$$\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1) := \langle \mathcal{O}_{Y_1},\, \mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(H) \rangle^{\perp} \subset \mathcal{D}^b(Y_1),$$
i.e. the right orthogonal of the exceptional pair $(\mathcal{O}_{Y_1}, \mathcal{O}_{Y_1}(H))$. Let $S_{\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)}$ be the Serre functor of $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$. Recall that a Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma$ on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ is called Serre-invariant if $S_{\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)} \cdot \sigma$ lies in the orbit of $\sigma$ under the action of $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$, the universal cover of $\mathrm{GL}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$, on the space of stability conditions.

Question: Do all Serre-invariant Bridgeland stability conditions on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ form a single orbit under the action of $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$?
status_search_result: For prime Fano threefolds $Y_d$ of index two and degree $2\le d\le 5$, uniqueness of the $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}_2^+(\mathbb{R})$-orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_d)$ has been established via the fractional Calabi–Yau criterion of Feyzbakhsh–Pertusi and Pertusi–Yang. For $d=1$ (the Veronese double cone), recent work on categorical Torelli theorems for weighted hypersurfaces explicitly mentions that the orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ is not known to be unique and that this is a motivation for using Hochschild–Serre algebra methods instead. No definitive proof of uniqueness or non-uniqueness for $\mathrm{Ku}(Y_1)$ was located, so the status is reported as unknown.

context_brief: Birational categorical Torelli for Gushel-Mukai threefolds
original_question: Let X1 and X2 be prime Fano threefolds of index 1 and degree 10, so in particular Gushel-Mukai threefolds. If there is a Fourier-Mukai type equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2), must X1 and X2 be birational?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be smooth prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one, index one, and degree ten over the complex numbers (so in particular each $X_i$ is a Gushel–Mukai threefold). For a smooth Gushel–Mukai threefold $X$, the bounded derived category $D^b(X)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$ D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X),\, \mathcal{E},\, \mathcal{O}_X \rangle, $$
where $\mathcal{E}$ is the rank-two tautological subbundle (pulled back from the Grassmannian under the Gushel embedding) and $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is the Kuznetsov component defined as the right orthogonal $\langle \mathcal{E}, \mathcal{O}_X \rangle^{\perp}$. Suppose that there exists an exact equivalence of triangulated categories
$$ \Phi : \mathcal{K}u(X_1) \longrightarrow \mathcal{K}u(X_2) $$
that is of Fourier–Mukai type (i.e., induced by a kernel object in $D^b(X_1 \times X_2)$ in the appropriate sense for admissible subcategories). Must $X_1$ and $X_2$ be birational?
status_search_result: Recent work (Jacovskis–Lin–Liu–Zhang and related papers) establishes that for smooth Gushel–Mukai threefolds, an equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(X_1)\simeq\mathcal{K}u(X_2)$ implies that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are period partners or duals, and hence birational, confirming the Kuznetsov–Perry birational categorical Torelli conjecture in this case. The question therefore appears affirmatively resolved.

context_brief: Categorical Torelli questions for quartic threefolds
original_question: For quartic threefolds, is there a categorical Torelli theorem, and does a birational categorical Torelli theorem hold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth quartic threefold, i.e. a smooth hypersurface of degree $4$. Its bounded derived category of coherent sheaves admits the semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X),\, \mathcal{O}_X,\, \mathcal{O}_X(1),\, \mathcal{O}_X(2),\, \mathcal{O}_X(3)\rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is defined as the right orthogonal complement
$$\mathcal{K}u(X) := \langle \mathcal{O}_X,\, \mathcal{O}_X(1),\, \mathcal{O}_X(2),\, \mathcal{O}_X(3)\rangle^{\perp} \subset D^b(X).$$

Address the following two questions for smooth quartic threefolds.

(a) (Categorical Torelli.) Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be two smooth quartic threefolds in $\mathbb{P}^4$. Suppose there exists a $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(X_1) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(X_2)$ (of Fourier–Mukai type). Does it follow that $X_1 \cong X_2$ as projective varieties? Identify, if necessary, the minimal additional hypotheses on the equivalence (or on $X_1$, $X_2$ in a general position sense) under which this implication holds.

(b) (Birational categorical Torelli.) Under the same hypothesis that $\mathcal{K}u(X_1) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(X_2)$, does it follow that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are birational over $\mathbb{C}$?

context_brief: Refined Torelli question for Gushel-Mukai fourfolds
original_question: Let X1 and X2 be Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, and suppose there is an equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) that commutes with the degree shift functors of X1 and X2. What additional assumptions on Phi are sufficient to conclude that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?
self_contained_problem:
A Gushel–Mukai (GM) fourfold is a smooth four-dimensional intersection $X = \mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \cap Q$, where $\mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is the projective cone over the Plücker embedding of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5) \subset \mathbb{P}^9$ and $Q \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is a quadric hypersurface. Equivalently, $X$ is a smooth projective fourfold of Picard rank one, index two, and degree ten admitting an embedding $X \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ (ordinary case) or a finite degree-two map to $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ (special case).

Let $\mathcal{O}_X$ denote the structure sheaf and $\mathcal{U}_X$ the rank-two tautological subbundle pulled back from $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$. The bounded derived category of coherent sheaves $D^b(X)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathrm{Ku}(X),\, \mathcal{O}_X,\, \mathcal{U}_X^{\vee},\, \mathcal{O}_X(1),\, \mathcal{U}_X^{\vee}(1) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ is a non-commutative K3 category (its Serre functor is the shift $[2]$ and its Hochschild homology agrees with that of a K3 surface).

The degree shift functor of $X$ is the autoequivalence $\sigma_X : \mathrm{Ku}(X) \to \mathrm{Ku}(X)$ obtained as the composition of the spherical twist along a natural spherical functor with tensoring by $\mathcal{O}_X(1)$ (equivalently, the restriction to $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ of the rotation autoequivalence associated to the Lefschetz decomposition above).

Problem. Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be Gushel–Mukai fourfolds and let
$$\Phi : \mathrm{Ku}(X_1) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{Ku}(X_2)$$
be a $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence such that $\Phi \circ \sigma_{X_1} \cong \sigma_{X_2} \circ \Phi$. Determine sufficient conditions on $\Phi$ (for instance, conditions on the induced map on numerical/Mukai lattices, on Bridgeland stability data, on Hodge structures, or further compatibility constraints) ensuring that $X_1 \cong X_2$ as algebraic varieties.
status_search_result: Categorical Torelli-type questions for Gushel–Mukai fourfolds remain an active research topic. Surveys on categorical Torelli theorems list the problem as open, and unlike the cubic fourfold case (where compatibility with the degree shift functor suffices for a categorical Torelli result), for GM fourfolds the situation is subtler: Hodge-association is known to be strictly stronger than homological association, so a precise sufficient condition on $\Phi$ guaranteeing isomorphism of GM fourfolds has not been established.

paper_title: Infrared tip-tilt sensing: on-sky experience, lessons learned and unsolved problems
original_question: What spot-displacement and loop-control algorithms can make an infrared tip-tilt sensor produce stable, accurate tip-tilt estimates when the adaptive-optics correction gives only a low-Strehl, partially corrected point-spread function, especially for off-axis guide stars where anisoplanatism broadens the spot and a diffraction-limited core can break into multiple time-varying speckles? The algorithm must avoid the increased noise of reading larger detector regions for centroiding and avoid simply tracking the brightest speckle, because that speckle can change with time and yield an inaccurate tip-tilt estimate.
status_search_result: The problem is identified within the adaptive-optics literature as an unresolved research challenge: optimal spot-displacement algorithms for low-Strehl, partially corrected PSFs in infrared tip-tilt sensing are explicitly listed as open. No published algorithm has been demonstrated to be optimal in this regime; centroiding for partially corrected off-axis PSFs remains an active research topic in extreme/wide-field AO instrumentation development.

paper_title: Infrared tip-tilt sensing: on-sky experience, lessons learned and unsolved problems
original_question: How should a laser-guide-star adaptive-optics system combine two or more off-axis infrared tip-tilt measurements to estimate the on-axis tip-tilt when the guide stars have different magnitudes, are measured at different frame rates, and have different centroiding errors caused by both photon count and spot shape? The desired solution should go beyond a weighted average by using tomography or an equivalent controller or reconstructor that can work for single-conjugate adaptive optics or laser-tomography adaptive optics.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a laser-guide-star adaptive-optics (AO) system on a large ground-based telescope, in either single-conjugate (SCAO) or laser-tomography (LTAO) configuration. Because a sodium or Rayleigh laser-guide star is insensitive to global tip and tilt (the two lowest-order Zernike modes corresponding to angular displacement of the wavefront), the on-axis tip-tilt component of the wavefront aberration must be measured from one or more off-axis natural guide stars (NGSs), typically in the near-infrared.

Setup. Suppose K ≥ 2 NGSs at angular positions θ_1, …, θ_K relative to the science target are available. For each star k:
- the apparent magnitude m_k (and hence photon flux) differs across stars;
- the tip-tilt sensor for star k is read out at its own frame rate f_k (chosen so that enough photons are integrated per frame);
- each centroid measurement y_k(t) ∈ ℝ^2 of the two-axis image position has measurement noise with covariance R_k that depends both on the photon count per frame and on the shape (size, elongation, asymmetry) of the point-spread function on the detector;
- the relation between the on-axis tip-tilt α(t) ∈ ℝ^2 to be estimated and y_k(t) is governed by the atmospheric tip-tilt anisoplanatism kernel determined by the C_n^2(h) profile and the offsets θ_k.

Model the time evolution of the atmospheric tip-tilt and the off-axis tip-tilts as a (possibly multi-layer) stochastic process with known second-order statistics (e.g., a Kolmogorov / von Kármán turbulence model with given outer scale L_0 and layer wind velocities), so that the joint process {α(t), (y_k(t))_k} is wide-sense stationary with computable spatio-temporal covariances.

Problem. Construct a real-time controller/reconstructor 𝒦 that takes as input the asynchronous, multi-rate streams (y_k(t_{k,j}))_{k,j} and produces an on-axis tip-tilt estimate α̂(t) (or equivalent control command for the tip-tilt mirror) which is optimal in the minimum-mean-square-error sense, generalizing the simple inverse-noise-variance weighted average. Specifically:

(a) Derive a tomographic minimum-variance reconstructor that simultaneously accounts for (i) different magnitudes m_k, (ii) different sampling rates f_k, (iii) measurement-noise covariances R_k that depend on both photon count and spot shape, and (iv) tip-tilt anisoplanatism between the off-axis NGS directions θ_k and the science direction.

(b) Show how 𝒦 can be implemented in closed loop (where the deformable/tip-tilt mirror modifies the measurements) for both SCAO and LTAO architectures, and prove (or characterize) its optimality with respect to on-axis residual tip-tilt variance.

(c) Quantify the performance gain over the standard inverse-variance weighted average of the off-axis centroids as a function of the asterism geometry, the magnitude/frame-rate distribution {(m_k, f_k)}, and the turbulence profile.

A complete solution consists of an explicit reconstructor (filter equations or state-space controller), a proof of its optimality under the stated stochastic model, and a quantitative performance comparison.
status_search_result: Multi-rate, minimum-variance split-tomography reconstructors for LGS adaptive optics with dim NGS tip-tilt stars have been studied (e.g., Gilles–Wang for TMT NFIRAOS), giving partial solutions for specific instruments. However, a general optimal real-time controller that simultaneously handles multiple NGSs of different magnitudes, different frame rates, and centroid noise depending on PSF shape (not just photon count) for SCAO/LTAO remains an active and unresolved research problem.
